title: Stripe-affinity allocator and compact-safepoint playbook for KV cache fragmentation mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: our KV cache continues to exhibit long-lived fragmentation on high-concurrency workloads (many short chats + mixed sequence lengths). Fragmentation increases per-token costs and occasionally causes suboptimal eviction storms that spike tail latency or trigger failover to slower model variants. Goal: implement a low-risk, incremental allocator + background compaction choreography that reduces long tail fragmentation without materially affecting generation latency or batch throughput. Approach summary: 1) introduce a stripe-affinity allocation layer that slices per-GPU KV pools into many micro-stripes and pins entries to stripes based on request fingerprint and temporal locality heuristics; 2) maintain per-stripe soft/hard watermarks and fast local eviction policies to avoid global compaction for small churn; 3) implement compact-safepoints (coordinated low-impact windows) where we perform relocation/compaction of hot holes using hop-buffered moves and cooperative throttling with the continuous-batcher; 4) expose fragmentation telemetry and relocation cost metrics to Console for rollouts and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end e2e benchmark showing at least 30% reduction in fragmentation ratio (free-holes bytes / total KV bytes) on mixed short-and-long sequence workload compared to baseline
No >5ms increase in median generation latency for steady-state serving during background compaction at default throttling settings
Relocation/compaction aborts safely rollback without data loss and do not cause OOMs under 99th percentile load
Console dashboard includes new fragmentation metric, hole-age histogram, and relocation cost-per-token; alerts for fragmentation_ratio > 0.18 for >10m

notes: Stripe sizing heuristics: target stripe capacity so that expected in-flight entries per stripe is small (10-100) to keep local compaction cheap; compute from median working set per model and tokens/sec distribution.
Per-stripe watermarks: soft_watermark triggers local eviction; hard_watermark prevents new pins and surfaces backpressure to request router/batcher.

Compaction safepoints: scheduled during observed micro-idle windows (low request rate for a GPU) or opportunistically inside low-priority batch slack; safepoint window is bounded to 200ms max per invocation to cap latency jitter.
Relocation protocol: hop-buffered move with pin-swap: allocate small temporary buffer in pinned host/GPU memory, copy source->temp->target, update metadata atomically; abort path restores pointers.
Cooperative throttling: credit-based system where batcher grants relocation credits proportional to current SLO slack. Credits consumed per byte moved; credits replenish with observed lower latency.
Size-aware lanes: large KV entries (top 5% by size) are isolated into dedicated stripes to avoid blocking many small relocations.
Failure modes and mitigation: if relocation fails mid-way, mark target slot quarantined and schedule async healing; ensure quarantined slots do not count against free capacity until healed.
Upgrade/rollback strategy: feature-flagged rollout with runtime flag to disable relocation on a per-GPU basis. Configurable thresholds in Console for aggressive/ conservative mode.
Telemetry plan: hole_age_histogram (buckets in seconds/minutes), fragmentation_ratio, relocation_bytes_per_minute, relocation_ops_per_minute, relocation_error_rate, allocator_meta_size_bytes.
Risk: small increase in 99.9th latency during heavy compaction spikes. Mitigation: aggressive throttling to zero and canary rollout; add automatic regression detection via perf guardrails.
